  "answer": "Mutual funds may avail intraday borrowing for all unitholder pay‑outs such as redemptions, IDCW pay‑outs, interest etc. [1] They may also use it for pay‑ins with respect to investments made by the scheme. [1] Intraday borrowings can be used to meet MTM obligations and foreign‑exchange settlements. [2] They may be employed for repayment of existing borrowings. [2] Additionally, intraday borrowing may be availed solely for the purpose of meeting redemption and other pay‑outs to unitholders as specified under Regulation 42(1) of the SEBI (Mutual Funds)
The intraday borrowing conditions apply from September 1 2026.[3][1]
The cost of intraday borrowing is borne by the AMC.[1]

No, a mutual fund may not borrow more than twenty per cent of the net assets of a scheme; borrowing is limited to a maximum of 20% of the scheme’s net assets, except for intraday borrowing which is permitted under separate conditions. This borrowing limit and the related provisions became effective on 1 April 2026.[4]

A Large Cap Fund must invest at least 80% of its total assets in large‑cap stocks.[1]
The scheme must have at least 20 investors, and no single investor may hold more than 25% of the scheme’s corpus [1].

The certification examination for mutual fund distributors is conducted by the National Institute of Securities Markets (NISM) [1]. This requirement is effective from 1 April 2026 as per the Master Circular for Mutual Funds [1].

The Master Circular for Mutual Funds issued on 20 March 2026 (HO/24/13/11(1)2026‑IMD‑POD‑1/I/7602/2026) is the one currently in force, having come into effect on 1 April 2026 and replacing the earlier circular dated 27 June 2024.[1][3]

The July 10 2026 circular superseded the earlier guidelines on borrowings of mutual funds – specifically the provisions in clause 5.9.1 of the SEBI Master Circular for Mutual Funds dated 20 March 2026 and the SEBI Circular HO/(92)2026‑IMD‑POD‑2/I/7885/2026 dated 25 March 2026[4].

The Gazette Notification dated July 3 2026 amended the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026 to allow mutual funds to undertake intraday borrowings for various purposes as outlined in the circular.[1]
